comment: Curated code ranges and RAM symbols. End addresses are exclusive. 'more' lists additional blocks for a routine page. 'caller_blocks' lists code reviewed for incoming references outside the documented routines.

routines.name: Frame tick: clock, shield and fuel
routines.summary: A BCD counter at $0340 counts 50 frames to a second, then the BCD clock at $0341-$0343 advances. When $0396 is zero, the shield regenerates and the routine updates the fuel at $0345/$0346. In the air it subtracts (speed >> 3) + 16, plus 96 for a ruptured tank. At altitude zero it subtracts 96 for a ruptured tank or 256 for an intact tank because the computed zero burn takes the same carry path. A high byte of $20 raises the LOW FUEL flag. On underflow the routine clears only the high byte and increments $03A3.

routines.name: New-game state reset
routines.summary: Clears the counters, clock and target pointers, then lays out a fresh ship at $57F0: altitude 28, shield and fuel full ($BF), eight missiles, flares and AMMs, laser heat zero.

routines.name: Low-fuel watch and the stranded state
routines.summary: Called every frame. Queues LOW FUEL once when $03A2 is set and NO FUEL once when $03A3 is set. If the tank is empty, altitude and speed are both zero, it sets $0396 to 1; LAUNCH treats that stranded state differently from a normal dock ($0396 = $80).

routines.name: Object distance and the docking test
routines.summary: Works out the distance to the record in $61/$62, scales it through the tables at $C800/$C900 and stores the product in bytes 12/13. Only a product under 128 is close enough to dock; anything up to 4,095 is added to the target list, and anything larger is dropped. For a close record, type 16 docks as a jump pad before anything else. A dockable building must pass |altitude - 28| + 55 < aperture, then a bearing test of 2 * (|bearing offset| + 28) against the same aperture - at the full 72-point opening that is an offset of at most 7 steps of the 512-step circle, about 5 degrees. Passing both sets $0396 = $80 and copies the building's type and cell to $03A4/$0398/$0399.

routines.name: City loader: the sheet at $9400 into the record table
routines.summary: Rebuilds the 48-record table at $0E00 for the city index in $0354. The pointer builder at $27EC multiplies the index by three and then shifts right three times, which is exactly a stride of 96 bytes: $9400 + city × $60. The loop copies up to 32 three-byte records (type, x, y) from that sheet, stopping at a type byte of $C0, zeroes bytes 3-15 of each record, and copies hit points from $C3BF[type & $3F] into byte 7. It then scans the city's four bytes at $8900, which hold jump destinations (a byte of $80 or more is empty), and appends a pair of pad records for each one from the four shared templates at $C4BE + n × 8. Whatever space is left in the table is filled with type $C0, and the provocation latch at $03BF is cleared.

routines.name: City save: writing damage back to the sheet
routines.summary: Called before a jump ($51C5) and from $6A77. Walks the city sheet at $9400 and the loaded record table at $0E00 in step, copying one byte per record — byte 0 — from the record back into the sheet. Types whose flags at $C39A hold both the mobile and armed bits ($60: types 3, 6, 9, 20 and 21) are skipped, so the armed mobile units always return. A destroyed building has already been marked type | $80 by the dying animation, so it is written back as free and stays destroyed on the next visit.

routines.name: City restore: stripping the state bits
routines.summary: Called by the new-game reset at $5863. Walks all twelve pages of the city sheet area from $9400 and masks every byte that is not $C0 with $3F, clearing the $80 and $40 state bits from every record. Since a destroyed record keeps its type under the free bit, this restores every city exactly: $93 becomes $13 again. The $C0 fillers are skipped because masking them would create type-0 buildings.

routines.name: Record scan
routines.summary: Walks the 48 sixteen-byte records at $0E00-$10FF. Byte 0 sorts them: $80 is free and skipped, $40 is dying and goes to the death animation, anything else is live and goes to the dispatcher at $445D. At the end of the sweep the game rotates the 6-bit round-robin index at $038F and advances its frame counters.

routines.name: Dying animation
routines.summary: Byte 6 falls by 8 a frame; when it reaches zero, byte 8 climbs by 8 a frame. At $F8 the record is freed. Types carrying bit 0 of $C39A (including both missile types) are freed at $78 instead, after 15 frames rather than 31.

routines.name: Live-record dispatch
routines.summary: Sorts a live record by its per-type flags at $C39A. Dockable types (bit 7) go to the aperture and docking path at $4465; sensor types (bit 1) are counted when in range at $44A1; everything else falls through to the guided-object and robot handlers.

routines.name: Aperture animation
routines.summary: Dockable buildings only, and only while byte 3 bit 6 says the record is active. A missile lock (bit 4) or a hit (bit 5) shuts the iris two points a frame, except on type 27; otherwise it shuts while the scaled distance byte 13 is 2 or more, and opens two points a frame to $48 while byte 13 is below 2. The door takes 36 frames to travel from shut to fully open.

routines.name: Sensor records
routines.summary: For records whose type flags carry bit 1. An in-range sensor (byte 3 bit 6, distance under 9 cells) is counted at $0373 and sets bit 7 of $03B0, which is what the scanner uses to know a contact is live.

routines.name: Guided-object handling
routines.summary: Reached from the dispatcher when a live record is neither dockable nor a sensor. Missiles and other guided objects take their target from bytes 14/15, publish their state to the eight-byte block at $FFC0, and run the homing and detonation logic that follows.

routines.name: Robot dispatch
routines.summary: A live record that is out of range has its moved/aimed bits cleared and is left alone. In range, the type flags choose the brain: bit 6 calls the static defence AI at $81F3, bit 5 calls the mobile unit AI at $80C3.

routines.name: Clear all missiles (AMM)
routines.summary: Walks the record table and marks every missile record dying - the player's type 10 and the robots' type 11 alike. Nothing else is touched: the selected target in $0388/$0389 survives, as does the target's lock bit. Both missile types are freed after 15 frames.

routines.name: Player missile launch
routines.summary: Refuses to fire at $0389 = 0 (no target). Otherwise finds a free record, makes it type 10, copies the ship's cell and sub-cell, sets byte 6 to altitude + $40, points bytes 14/15 at the target, sets the target's lock bit (byte 3 bit 4) and decrements the missile count at $0358.

routines.name: Damage
routines.summary: Shared by lasers and everything else. Subtracts the damage in A from byte 7. On underflow it clears byte 8, sets the death sound counter, marks byte 0 dying, and for armed types adds one to the 16-bit kill count at $03A5/$03A6. Finally it sets $0359 = $FF for the screen flash. A record whose byte 7 is already negative is immune.

routines.name: Laser fire
routines.summary: Checks that no bolt is in flight ($036E), heat is below $B0 and the laser is enabled ($0370), then checks the fire input. Firing sets the bolt timer to $80, latches provocation in $03BF, requests the shot sound and adds $0C to the heat at $0347, capped at $BF. The target is tested later when the bolt finishes.

routines.name: Laser bolt: timer and hit
routines.summary: Counts the bolt's flight in the low seven bits of $036E. At 22 frames it clears the bolt colour, resets $036E and resolves the shot against $038C/$038D: exactly one target, only if still alive, takes 4 points through the damage routine at $4951 and gets byte 3 bit 5 set.

routines.name: Flag-bit test
routines.summary: Tests one bit of the eight-byte mask at $034A-$0351. A holds the bit index: X = A >> 3 selects the byte from $034A, and the low three bits index the mask table at $3D28. Returns with Z set when the bit is clear.

routines.name: Static defence AI
routines.summary: Static defence AI. Type flags bit 5 (mobile units) always run; everyone else runs only while the provocation latch $03BF is set. Out of class range it does nothing. In range it sets byte 3 bit 3, answers a player lock with an AMM after 24 frames (clearing its own lock first), and otherwise counts byte 9 against the fire interval at $C45E. A random roll masked by $C44E reloads the counter; behaviour bit 7 units also roll against $C46E and, on success, take a free record from $1000 and spawn a missile into it. Type 26 has an early path of its own at $8202. Movement ends at $8347.

routines.name: Mobile unit AI
routines.summary: Dispatched from $4620 for records whose type flags carry bit 5. Types 36 and 21 bob between two altitudes first, flipping byte 3 bit 0; every mobile then runs the class-range test, closes on the ship and fires. Out of range it clears byte 8 and returns.

routines.name: Message queue
routines.summary: Pushes a two-byte text pointer into the ring buffer at $0C00: A is the low byte, X the high, and $0384 is the write cursor. Does not print; the printer drains the queue separately.

routines.name: Message text renderer
routines.summary: Reads one character code at a time from the pointer in $1C/$1D. Codes under $80 select an 8-byte glyph from the game's own font at $9000-$92FF (32 glyphs a page); $80 is a control code, and $FF ends the string. The glyph is copied into the character/sprite buffer at $FCC8.

variables.name: Launch heading (low)
variables.doc: Low eight bits of the ship's heading. LAUNCH adds $20 - 32 steps of 512, or 22.5 degrees - and carries into $0339.

variables.name: Launch heading (high)
variables.doc: Ninth bit of the heading; toggled on launch so the 22.5-degree step wraps correctly.

variables.name: Frame counter
variables.doc: BCD counter of frames within the second, 0-$49. At $50 the clock ticks.

variables.name: Seconds
variables.doc: BCD seconds, 0-$59.

variables.name: Minutes
variables.doc: BCD minutes, 0-$59.

variables.name: Hours
variables.doc: BCD hours, 0-$23.

variables.name: Altitude
variables.doc: 0-$BF. Zero is the ground; docking altitude is 28 ($1C).

variables.name: Fuel (low byte)
variables.doc: Low byte of the 16-bit fuel value. The burn routine keeps the low-byte result even when an underflow clears the high byte.

variables.name: Fuel (whole units)
variables.doc: High byte of the fuel value. Full is $BF, just under 192 units; LAUNCH refuses at zero.

variables.name: Laser heat
variables.doc: 0-$BF. Each shot adds $0C; at $B0 or above the laser will not fire.

variables.name: Flag mask
variables.doc: Eight bytes, 64 bits, tested by the helper at $3D18.

variables.name: Speed
variables.doc: 0-$BF. Divided by 8 to get the fuel burn, and tested for zero when deciding the ship is at rest.

variables.name: Missiles
variables.doc: Missile count, eight at the start of a game; decremented by a launch.

variables.name: Bolt timer
variables.doc: Zero when the laser is ready. Firing sets $80; the low seven bits then count the bolt's 22-frame flight.

variables.name: Laser lockout
variables.doc: While non-zero the laser cannot fire.

variables.name: Shield
variables.doc: 0-$BF, full at the start of a game. Regenerates one point a second while airborne and not docked.

variables.name: Dock refused
variables.doc: Set to $FF when a docking attempt fails the altitude or aim test.

variables.name: Message read cursor
variables.doc: Next slot in the $0C00 ring buffer to print.

variables.name: Message write cursor
variables.doc: Next slot in the $0C00 ring buffer to fill.

variables.name: Last on-screen target
variables.doc: Viewport candidate whose projected width reaches the centre columns. The painter copies it to $0388/$0389 after finishing its pass.

variables.name: Missile target
variables.doc: Pointer the missile launch routine reads. Zero means no lock; cleared on a new game and after a jump.

variables.name: Viewport laser candidate
variables.doc: Candidate set by the tighter raster test at $30F2. The painter copies it to $038C/$038D after finishing its pass.

variables.name: Laser target
variables.doc: Pointer resolved when the bolt lands; the hit goes to this record and no other.

variables.name: Dock state
variables.doc: 0 in flight, $80 after a normal dock, 1 when stranded with an empty tank on the ground.

variables.name: Docked cell (low)
variables.doc: Low byte of the docked building's cell, copied on docking and used as the ship's position on launch.

variables.name: Docked cell (high)
variables.doc: High byte of the docked building's cell.

variables.name: Jump pad docked
variables.doc: Set to $FF when the docked building is type 16, the jump pad.

variables.name: Tank ruptured
variables.doc: Non-zero adds 96 to the per-second fuel burn.

variables.name: LOW FUEL flag
variables.doc: Set once when the fuel high byte reaches $20; the watch routine prints the message for value 1 and then increments it.

variables.name: NO FUEL flag
variables.doc: Set when fuel underflows. Also drives the stranded state on the ground.

variables.name: Docked type
variables.doc: Record byte 0 of the docked building, copied at $2C4E.

variables.name: Kill count (low)
variables.doc: Incremented by the damage routine for every armed type destroyed.

variables.name: Kill count (high)
variables.doc: High byte of the kill count.

variables.name: Provocation latch
variables.doc: Set by a laser ($341E) or a missile launch ($48F6) and cleared when a city loads. Static defences ignore the ship until it is set.
